correctness.rationale: Coprimality to 6 means a unit modulo 36, and gcd(s,36)=6 gives precisely the residues 6 and 30. Multiplication by a unit preserves that gcd and subsequence length; after normalization and sorting, any counterexample is a nondecreasing multiset starting with 1. Each recurrence state records sums of exactly j selected positions; the update takes old j−1 sums to account for inclusion of the new position, so repeats of a residue are handled correctly, and a pruned prefix cannot have a bad extension. An independent 36-bit-mask search with no depth cap reproduced all 3944 admissible prefixes, with counts 1,10,47,141,322,560,638,639,633,566,315,72 by length and no length-13 state. For the lower bound, d+13e with −5≤d≤5 and e∈{−1,0,1} cannot equal ±6 modulo 36, even without any length restriction. Thus 13 suffices for the short version and is necessary for the unrestricted version, proving both equalities.
residual_risks: The exhaustion is for modulus 6 only; it does not classify all twelve-term extremizers or settle other moduli.

evidence: The distinct same-day Finding gives s1(6)=13 for arbitrary nonmultiples of 6 and exactly six terms, with a divisible-by-6/not-divisible-by-36 target.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The identical numerical value in the Resultary Finding is for a different invariant. In particular it is possible to encounter a weak target but no exact target: (1,1,1,1,1,7) has six-term sum 12 but no exact-gcd-6 subsequence.

originality.rationale: The prior exact-gcd problem and the twelve-term witness are verified in Gao–Jiang–Mu. The supported distinct claim is the matching upper bound at n=6. The strongest numerically similar same-day finding and the published weaker-predicate theorem neither guarantee a sum with gcd exactly 6 nor imply this upper bound.
residual_risks: The bounded review cannot rule out an unindexed solution or another upper-bound result stated under a different formulation.

value.rationale: The first modulus with two distinct prime divisors is the natural boundary of the known prime-power theorem and the first instance of the cited problem, not an arbitrary experimental choice. A sharp upper bound for the more restrictive short-subsequence invariant shows that the general lower construction is attained already at this boundary and settles both thresholds there.
residual_risks: The contribution establishes the first case by finite exhaustion; it supplies neither a general composite-modulus method nor all extremizers.
